sections.title: The Writing on the Wall
observations: In this chapter, we witness a dramatic shift in the narrative of Daniel. King Belshazzar, the last king of Babylon, throws a lavish feast, using the sacred vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem. This act of sacrilege sets the stage for divine judgment.

The appearance of the mysterious hand writing on the wall serves as a powerful symbol of God's sovereignty and judgment. It is a stark reminder that no earthly power can stand against the will of God.

sections.title: Daniel's Interpretation
observations: Belshazzar's panic leads him to seek out Daniel, who had previously interpreted dreams for Nebuchadnezzar. This highlights the continuity of God's message through His chosen servant, despite the changing rulers.

Daniel's interpretation of the writing—'Mene, Mene, Tekel, Parsin'—reveals God's judgment against Belshazzar for his arrogance and blasphemy. Each term carries significant meaning, emphasizing the finality of God's decree.

sections.title: The Fall of Babylon
observations: The chapter concludes with the fulfillment of Daniel's interpretation as Belshazzar is slain, and the Medes and Persians take over Babylon. This event marks the end of an era and serves as a historical reminder of God's control over nations and rulers.
The suddenness of Belshazzar's downfall illustrates the theme of divine sovereignty and the transient nature of human power.

importantVerses.commentary: This verse contains the mysterious writing on the wall, which serves as the central message of God's judgment against Belshazzar.
Daniel interprets the writing, declaring that Belshazzar has been weighed and found wanting, emphasizing the theme of divine justice.

questions: What does the writing on the wall signify in the context of God's judgment?
How does Belshazzar's behavior reflect the attitudes of those in positions of power today?
What lessons can we learn from the fall of Babylon regarding the sovereignty of God over nations?
